entry_state: PPE preparation, replacement and revaluation require cost purpose, availability and asset-specific histories, with separate profit, OCI and cash consequences. Employee benefits retain actuarial inputs and avoid duplicating plan-paid benefits as employer cash. The impairment example has allocated loss 50 to goodwill 20, asset A 5 and asset B 25, respecting floors; the iterative allocation discussion continues next.
exit_state: Impairment allocation preserves individual floors and a finite residual, while reversal respects the depreciated no-impairment path and excludes goodwill. A zero-weight reversal remains unresolved rather than receiving invented weights. Provisions require an existing duty and supported measurement. The factory case now asks why low output cannot load all idle-capacity cost into its remaining goods.
findings: The capped allocation states positive weights and records a capacity shortfall without inventing a balancing liability or asserting jointly coherent valuations.
The reversal example recognizes 24 rather than the requested 34, retains goodwill at zero and reconciles PPE 80 with the depreciation and allowance histories.
The fully zero-weight reversal is expressly unresolved; finite arithmetic does not close that method gap.
Provision recognition distinguishes an existing obligation from future intended spending. No new confirmed exposition defect on these pages.
